newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai stock indices end up on speculation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai stock indices end up on speculation.

text.p: Shanghai's A and B share indices closed up sharply on Friday on active domestic speculative buying on the belief that the death of Deng Xiaoping has removed a major negative factor on the stock markets, brokers said.
The B index rose 0.894 points or 1.38 percent to 65.569 points on volume of 30.4 million shares worth $13.5 million against Thursday's $17.1 million.

The domestic A share index closed at a year high of 1063.276 points, rising 55.545 points or 5.51 percent, on volume of 1.3 billion shares worth 10.7 billion yuan, up from eight billion yuan on Thursday.
Brokers said market sentiment was steady after the death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping, but many overseas investors were seen liquidating their positions on concerns about firms' results.
"Domestic speculative funds mainly from Shenzhen boosted the A share market, which in turn supported the B share market," one broker said.
"Most investors believe China's economy will remain stable despite Deng's death," a second broker said.
Of 43 B shares, 42 traded, with 30 up, four flat and eight down.
Shanghai Goods & Materials Trade Centre was the star on speculative buying, surging $0.016 or 9.52 percent to $0.184 on volume of 187,200 shares.
Textile machinery maker Shanghai Erfangji followed on rumours of financial restructuring, jumping $0.014 or 8.53 percent to $0.178 on the day's heaviest volume of 3.5 million shares.
On the A share market, the SSE 30 blue-chip index closed up 124.904 points or 4.73 percent to 2767.037 points.
Yunnan Baoshan Cement was the star, surging 0.56 yuan to limit-up of 6.11 yuan on volume of 2.6 million shares.
